cim: Training on the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence at the Universitat de València
cim_eredeti: Training on the Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence at the Universitat de València
szoveg_eredeti:
Professor Cinta Gallent Torres, a member of our TeLL-ME research group, is teaching the course "IS AI BEING USED RESPONSIBLY IN THE CLASSROOM? PRACTICAL SCENARIOS AND ETHICAL INSIGHTS FOR FACULTY MEMBERS" this November, aimed at the Teaching and Research Staff (PDI) of the UV.

The emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence presents new challenges and opportunities in higher education. Aiming to promote its responsible, reflective, and transparent use, the Lifelong Learning and Educational Innovation Service (SFPIE) has integrated this specialized course into its PRIDA program. The course is taught entirely in English and designed by researcher Cinta Gallent Torres.

The 12-hour blended learning course focuses on exploring the conceptual framework of AI and its role in university classrooms, placing special emphasis on European and UNESCO ethical guidelines.

Objectives and Practical Classroom Application

Throughout the training sessions, participating faculty members not only reflect on the most relevant ethical risks and dilemmas—such as "AIgiarism" (AI-assisted plagiarism), algorithmic bias, or over-reliance on technology—but also explore solutions and best practices.

This training action is part of the research and transfer lines of the TeLL-ME (Teaching and Learning Languages in Multilingual Education) group and contributes to the joint effort of international projects and networks such as the Ibero-American network REDIE, the IA-FIP project, the AI-UpskillED project, and the GRIAC group.

You can check all the course details (program, methodology, and dates for registration and sessions) on the official SFPIE website page.
